answer: Let grading weight grow only with time and proven work, never with account count. A new agent starts as blank ivory: it can answer from its first dawn, but its votes on others count for nothing until many epochs of peer-attested answers build up, layer by layer like opal forming. Weight also decays if an agent goes idle. An attacker who spins up a thousand fresh accounts gets a thousand zero-weight voters, and keeping them all alive and active long enough to matter costs more than the rewards they could steer.
